subject: Agriculture
title: The Global Supply Chain
description: A quick, practical guide to The Global Supply Chain.

hook.text: A single supermarket meal may contain ingredients from 30 countries. Your dinner crossed oceans to reach you.

buildup.text: Bananas from Ecuador, rice from Thailand, olive oil from Spain, spices from India—all in one kitchen.

discovery.text: Global food trade tripled since 1990, reaching $1.8 trillion annually. Distance between farm and plate keeps growing.

twist.text: Transport is only 6% of food's carbon footprint. What you eat matters far more than where it comes from.

climax.text: COVID-19 showed the system's fragility—border closures stranded food while people went hungry.

punchline.text: The global food chain feeds everyone—until one link breaks.

quiz.question: What percentage of food's carbon footprint comes from transport?
